_note: Tags, badges, archetypes and qualifications (docs/specs/TAGS_BADGES_ARCHETYPES_QUALIFICATIONS.md, master plan Phase 2). Every rule and number lives here; trainers/recognition.py and its browser copy (app/web/29_recognition.html) only evaluate them, and app/test_recognition_parity.mjs holds the two together. Recognition describes what the mechanics already do: no badge changes a fight (spec Part X). Status: provisional. The values are the spec's proposals, calibrated against the field in docs/recognition/CALIBRATION.md, for Zack to adjust.
_tiers: The labels the spec proposes (Part II §5). They're Zack's to rename (D-059); a badge can have fewer tiers than four.

stats._note: A stat's tier compares the stat at level 100 as built (its own nature, IVs and EVs) with what a Pokémon of base B reaches with full investment: IV 31, 252 EVs and a helpful nature (HP has no nature; Gen II: DV 15, maxed stat experience, no natures). The thresholds are computed from these bases, never typed in: in Gen IV they're the spec's 328 / 350 / 394 / 438, and HP 364 / 404 / 444 / 504. A build with no EVs recorded earns no stat tier (blank is no evidence, B19).

speed._note: Speed is about who it outruns. A milestone is one point above a base-B Pokémon at full investment with a +Speed nature (Gen IV level 100: 329, 351, 362, 373, 395). One point short is a tie, not an outspeed. Natural Speed, boosted Speed (Choice Scarf, +1 and +2, Swift Swim and Chlorophyll in their weather), paralysis, priority and Trick Room are kept apart: only natural Speed earns the Speed tiers.
speed.name: Speed

damage._note: From the Ace fights (trainers/team_roles.py evidence()): the Elite Four and Champion Pokémon of its generation, each set once, both level 100, the calculator's roll range at no boosts from full, every move landing, no critical hits. Guaranteed means the lowest roll does it; a 2HKO is two hits with nothing healed in between. Taking n hits means the top roll is under 100/(n-1)% of its HP.
damage.collection: elite_four + champion (team_roles.json → pools), each set once

physical_breaker.name: Physical Breaker
physical_breaker.says: its best physical attack ({move}) is a guaranteed {measure} on {share} of them ({n} of {of})

special_breaker.name: Special Breaker
special_breaker.says: its best special attack ({move}) is a guaranteed {measure} on {share} of them ({n} of {of})

priority_finisher.name: Priority Finisher
priority_finisher.says: {move} finishes {share} of them from {hp}% HP ({n} of {of})

physical_wall.name: Physical Wall
physical_wall.says: takes four or more of {share} of their physical attacks ({n} of {of})
physical_wall._note: A wall is judged by how many hits it takes, not by one hit from full (spec Part IV: Defense alone isn't walling): the share of their attacks whose top roll is under a third of its HP, the same four-hit standard as the team role Wall (D-060).

special_wall.name: Special Wall
special_wall.says: takes four or more of {share} of their special attacks ({n} of {of})

mixed_wall.name: Mixed Wall
mixed_wall.says: both walls, at the lower of the two tiers

damage._tiers: Tiers build on each other (a tier needs the ones below it) and sit near the 50th, 70th, 85th and 95th percentile of the stored builds that have that kind of attack (docs/recognition/CALIBRATION.md). The Elite Four's and Champions' Pokémon have no EVs and low IVs at level 100, so single-hit numbers saturate: walls count four hits, and a breaker's Elite tier asks for OHKOs.

kit._note: v2 (D-078): two badge families read from the build itself, the way competitive players read a set. Sustain: how it heals (best level reached: Bronze passive or draining, Silver Rest or Wish, Gold reliable recovery, Elite reliable recovery with Leftovers or Black Sludge). Utility: how many distinct support jobs its moves do (one job is Bronze, four is Elite). Names only, so both engines read them the same.

sustain.name: Sustain
says: heals half its HP with {moves}, and holds {item}

tags._note: Machine-readable descriptions, from the role engine's signals (trainers/roles.json; blank EVs never count, B19). A tag with a level carries that signal's 0-1 value.

qualifications._note: What a build has demonstrated against a standard. Ace is the established one (D-060, team_roles.json → roles.ace) and is read straight from the team roles; the other two are provisional and read from the same fights.

archetype._note: The functional archetype is the build name from the name ladder (team_roles.json → naming) when its match is at least ladder_at_least; below that, every build still gets one: the role engine's primary role, joined to its secondary when that one is close behind (a hybrid). Signature archetypes are a curated library on top; the functional one always stays underneath for filtering.

signature._note: Distinctive names for unusual, mechanically defined combinations (spec Part VII §13). None is on until Zack approves it: the ones here are proposals built from the spec's own examples, to react to, rename or delete. A signature never depends on being shiny, legendary or high-BST.

list.name: Steel Executioner
list.why: A Steel type that sets up and then finishes with priority: the spec's Technician Bullet Punch Scizor, defined by what it does rather than what it is.

list.name: Dragon Vanguard
list.why: A Dragon that boosts and outruns base-110 Speed while breaking through physically.

list.name: Unbreakable Sentinel
list.why: Survives nine in ten of the Elite Four's and Champions' attacks on both sides, and heals itself.

list.name: Phantom Striker
list.why: A fast Ghost whose special attacks 2HKO most of the field.

tier_names._note: v1 (D-077), the FIFA/2K idea: a stat-gated badge gets a name at each tier, so a Gold Speed badge reads as 'Blazing'. Display only: the badge, its tier and its threshold are unchanged, and nothing in battle reads these names. Yours to rename (A-55).
